name: Lake Como
tagline: Villas, gardens and a rationalist masterpiece, an hour from Milan.
distinctive: Lake Como pairs the grand villa gardens of its shoreline with something few lake resorts have: Como town's remarkable twentieth-century architecture. Mornings on the water, afternoons in gardens and a car for the hill roads make it complete.

image.alt: Illustration of Lake Como seen from a stone terrace, with cypresses and mountains beyond

moodNotes.sea: A lake rather than the sea, but mornings are spent on the water and villages are best reached by boat.
moodNotes.art: Villa gardens at Tremezzo and Bellagio, and Giuseppe Terragni's Casa del Fascio in Como town, a landmark of Italian rationalism.
moodNotes.lifetime: The lake's grand historic villa hotels make a first visit feel like an occasion.
moodNotes.weekend: Milan's airports are roughly an hour away, so a long weekend loses little time to travel.
moodNotes.wellness: Lakeside spas, quiet gardens and slow boat days make it a gentle place to rest.
moodNotes.drive: The western shore road and the hills above Menaggio reward an early start.

seasonNote: Many lakeside hotels close from roughly November to March; July and August are the busiest months.

arrival.transfer: Allow roughly an hour to an hour and a half by road from either Milan airport to the western shore, more at busy times.
arrival.groundNote: Lakeside roads are narrow and crowded in summer. Public ferries and private water taxis are often the more graceful way between villages.

driving.note: Rewarding outside peak weekends: the western shore and the climbs into the hills. Leave the car parked on the days you spend on the water.

carWhy: The lake is made for a slow open-top drive, and a grand tourer is just as comfortable for the motorway back to Milan.

transfer.label: Private boat between villages
transfer.why: Book a boat for the days in Bellagio and Tremezzo; it is quicker than the road and far more beautiful.

stay.name: Villa d'Este
stay.why: A historic villa hotel in large gardens on the water at Cernobbio. It is close to Como town for the architecture day and on the western shore for the drives.

watchWhy: The Reverso and Terragni's Casa del Fascio date from the same years between the wars. Both are exercises in rational, elegant geometry.
aromaWhy: Cypress, fig leaf and warm stone recall the lake's terraced gardens and are fresh enough for a warm car.

days.title: Arrive by water
days.text: Check in, then take a boat north along the western shore past the wooded headland of Villa del Balbianello. Dine by the lake as the light goes.

days.title: Como's rationalist heart
days.text: Spend a morning in Como town: the cathedral, then Giuseppe Terragni's Casa del Fascio on Piazza del Popolo, an architecture stop rather than a place to stay. Ride the funicular to Brunate for the view in the late afternoon.

days.title: Gardens of the mid-lake
days.text: See the gardens of Villa Carlotta at Tremezzo, cross to Bellagio by ferry, and have a late lunch. Drive the shore road home at sunset.

moreDays.title: Into the hills
moreDays.text: Drive up from Menaggio into the hills for mountain views and a long lunch well away from the waterfront.

moreDays.title: The eastern shore
moreDays.text: Take the ferry to Varenna for the gardens of Villa Monastero and a walk along the lakeside path.

moreDays.title: A slower day
moreDays.text: Spend the day at the spa and a lakeside lido, with nothing else planned.
